title: After Thunder Comes Rain
source: Diogenes Laertius, Lives of the Philosophers II.36 (Yonge tr.)
lesson: You can't control others' anger, only your response.
lines: Socrates had a wife named Xanthippe. She was famous in Athens for one thing: her temper.
Socrates spent all day asking people questions instead of earning money. Xanthippe was not impressed. Not even a little.
One day she shouted at him for an hour. A whole hour. The neighbours closed their windows. Socrates just sat there, calm as a mountain.
So she grabbed a bucket of water, and poured it right over his head!
Dripping wet, Socrates said: Well, I knew that after thunder, there would be rain.
You can't control other people's storms. But you can always choose how you respond to them. That's real strength.
Next time: Socrates gets kicked, and his reply is legendary. Follow so you don't miss it!
